# Product Owner Flow Templates

Copy/apply patterns for Product Owner Flow Mode models.

**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, with `references/flow-mode.md` whenever Flow intent is selected
**Purpose:** Provides the user-flow patterns, the provenance table every diagram type keeps and the reply shape every type delivers
**Scope:** Five user-flow patterns, the intake questions, the provenance table and the reply shape. The other types keep their patterns in `assets/templates/`
**Output Path:** None. The model is working data and the board is the deliverable

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Every pattern below passes `scripts/flow_check.py` as a user flow, and `scripts/compose_board.py` composes it into a board. Start from the pattern closest to the flow, rename the nodes after the real screens and triggers, add the board lines below and run the check before the write gate. A process, an architecture, a sequence, a state diagram, an ER diagram or a gantt chart starts from its own file in `assets/templates/`, and keeps the provenance table and the reply shape below.

### Usage

- Node ids are short, stable and camelCase, because the provenance table names them, the composer names every layer after them and the generated fallback mis-routes an underscore
- A label names the screen or the action a person takes, in the words the product uses, in one to four words where those words allow
- A label with a parenthesis, a colon or a slash goes in double quotes, such as `pick["Pick a plan (monthly)"]`
- A decision label is a question, and each exit label is one of its answers
- Every connector is a solid arrow `-->`
- A user flow and a process each carry exactly one `style` line, which marks the first glance. A styled goal, failing end or decision keeps its kind and takes a pink outline, and a styled step is drawn light pink. `style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575` makes that end the goal and the light red pair makes an end a failure. Every pair comes from `references/style-guide.md`, and any other colour is refused or counts as a second accent
- Write `flowchart LR` unless the chain is short, because a board reads wider than it reads tall

### Board lines

The board's own text rides on `%%` comment lines, which the check ignores and the composer reads. Each one is optional, and the generated fallback strips them all:

```text
%% title: Start a return
%% subtitle: How a customer starts a return in the app, from the order list to a confirmed return
%% source: Sources: five app screenshots and the returns doc. Left out: free pickup over 100 euros, a proposal.
%% zone: Find the order: orders, detail
%% zone: Request the return: window, reason, method
```

- `%% title:` names the board. With none, the composer takes a Mermaid frontmatter title, a sequence or gantt `title` line, then `Diagram <n>`
- `%% subtitle:` is one sentence under the title on who reads the board and why
- `%% source:` is the line under the key naming the sources and what was left out
- `%% zone: <label>: <id>, <id>` groups nodes in a tinted section. A user flow or a process without lanes reads its zones in flow order, and once a flow has zones every node sits in exactly one. An ER diagram draws each zone around its entities. Lanes and composite states are zones already, so a laned process, an architecture or a state diagram takes no zone line

---

## 2. PATTERNS

### Linear flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start([Open the page]) --> step1[Fill in the form]
    step1 --> step2[Submit]
    step2 --> done([Confirmation shown])
    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
```

### One decision

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start([Open the page]) --> step1[Submit the form]
    step1 --> valid{Valid?}
    valid -->|Yes| done([Confirmation shown])
    valid -->|No| fix[Show the field errors]
    fix --> step1
420:## 8. DELIVERY
421-
422-The reply carries the board, its proof and the self-scan, and nothing else. Anything the user must know or answer has a place above the self-scan.
423-
424-- The first line is the board URL
425-- The second line is the read-back, counts measured on the board against the model, in the words the type's reference uses: `Read-back: 8 of 8 nodes, 8 of 8 connectors, 2 of 2 decision exits labelled`. When the connected tools include no read tool, the line is `Read-back: not possible, the connector has no read tool`, and the board is never called done. When the board URL landed in a re-saved artifact, the line ends with the name of the file the artifact was saved to. On a matched read-back the same line also names the first glance in one clause, such as `, first glance: the failed payment`, so the user knows what should win before the board is opened
426-- When the write added extensions, the next line counts them: `Extensions: 4 of 4 pins, 4 of 4 legend stickies, 0 overlaps`, or `Extensions: 2 of 2 notes, 0 overlaps` for single stickies
427-- When the provenance table lists items left out, the next line names them as `Left out: <item>, <reason>`, so the user sees what the board does not hold. On a split or a cut, the reason names the detail level and the cut, such as `Left out: the retry path, split into a second diagram`
428-- A contradicted item appears in that same line with both of its sources and the reason it was not drawn, so a finding the sources disagree on is still visible to the reader
429-- When the file holds two or more diagrams, the read-back line also names the board a reader opens first, by the ordinal and the name in its title, in one clause such as `, start here: 1. Signup`
430-- A finding from the read-back, a warning the write returned, a `DESIGN` line the composer printed, an open item or a question the user must answer is one `Finding:` line each, placed above the self-scan. A `DESIGN` finding names the token, what the design file asked for and the value the board drew instead. Where the board landed, the tools used, the cleanup and the rollback are not part of the reply
431-- The last line is the HVR self-scan in the shape `AGENTS.md` step 8 sets, counted on the labels written to the board. Nothing follows it, not a note, a finding or a question. Flow Mode is exempt from the export steps, never from the scan
432-- A read-back that does not match is reported as measured, with the missing or extra items named. The board is never called done on a mismatch

content.text:
I've drafted the flow model and it passes the pre-write check. Nothing is written to Figma yet. Please check this outline before I set up the write.

**What the board answers:** how does a Fernhouse customer start a return in the app today?

**Model** (9 nodes, 9 connectors, passes the check with no crossings):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    orders([Order list]) --> detail[Order detail]
    detail --> window{Within 30 days of delivery?}
    window -->|No| support([Contact support])
    window -->|"Yes, Start a return"| reason[Pick a return reason]
    reason --> method{Drop-off or pickup?}
    method -->|Drop-off point| dropoff[Choose a drop-off point]
    method -->|Courier pickup| pickup[Book a courier pickup]
    dropoff --> done([Confirmation with QR code])
    pickup --> done
    style window fill:#FFC2EC,stroke:#F849C1
```

- **Sections:** *Find the order* (order list, detail, the 30-day check, Contact support), *Request the return* (reason, method) and *Hand it over* (drop-off, pickup, QR confirmation)
- **Highlighted step:** the 30-day check, because it decides whether a customer can return at all.

**Changes from what I proposed last time:**
- **Start a return** is now the label on the "Yes" arrow, not its own step. The check allows at most 9 nodes, and a separate step made 10.
- I'd moved the highlight from **Start a return** to the 30-day check, because **Start a return** is no longer a node. If you'd rather keep the highlight on **Start a return** as a node, I'll split the flow into two diagrams instead.
- The free pickup over €100 now goes in the board's source line as *proposal under review*, not as a note on the pickup step. A note would add an extra write to the board.

**Assumed** (you didn't send the screenshots or the returns doc):
- The screen order and labels come from your summary.
